runs.pr_body:
## median_cents returns the upper middle value instead of averaging the two middle values for even-length lists.

Closes: Fix median_cents for even-length amount lists

### Plan
- Read ledgerlite/stats.py to locate median_cents even-length branch
- Fix even-count case to average the two middle values so median_cents([100,200,300,400]) returns 250
- Add regression test covering even-count median in tests/test_stats_regression.py
- Run regression test and existing tests to verify fix

### Files changed
- ledgerlite/stats.py
- tests/test_stats_regression.py

### Tests
All tests pass (9 → 13 discovered).

### Reviewer
approve: Checked diff limited to ledgerlite/stats.py median fix and new tests/test_stats_regression.py with no unrelated changes; tests pass (9 to 13). Regression tests cover even-count averaging, unsorted input, half-value result, and odd-count unchanged behavior.
runs.diff:
diff --git a/ledgerlite/stats.py b/ledgerlite/stats.py
index 653bddb..b098585 100644
--- a/ledgerlite/stats.py
+++ b/ledgerlite/stats.py
@@ -22,4 +22,4 @@ def median_cents(values):
     mid = n // 2
     if n % 2 == 1:
         return ordered[mid]
-    return ordered[mid]  # BUG: even count must average ordered[mid-1] and ordered[mid]
+    return (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2

--- new file: tests/test_stats_regression.py ---
+import unittest
+
+from ledgerlite.stats import median_cents
+
+
+class TestMedianCentsEvenCountRegression(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_median_even_count_averages_two_middle_values(self):
+        self.assertEqual(median_cents([100, 200, 300, 400]), 250)
+
+    def test_median_even_count_unsorted_input(self):
+        self.assertEqual(median_cents([400, 100, 300, 200]), 250)
+
+    def test_median_even_count_may_be_half_value(self):
+        self.assertEqual(median_cents([100, 201]), 150.5)
+
+    def test_median_odd_count_unchanged(self):
+        self.assertEqual(median_cents([100, 200, 300]), 200)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
